## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The release gate must be fixed before merge: it now rejects a release that holds exactly the required number of approvals, which contradicts the module's stated contract and the base behaviour. The remaining two findings are optional corrections, and most of the catalog hunk was not read line by line.

## Changes
The pull request renames the 1500 catalog entries in `aaa-generated/catalog.json` from `legacy-service-NNNN` on ports 1NNNN to `production-service-NNNN` on ports 2NNNN and appends one extra top-level key. It also rewrites `healthy` in `services/registry.py` as `not failures` and changes the comparison in `approved` in `zzz-release/gate.py` from `>=` to `>`.

## Critical
- zzz-release/gate.py:5 — correctness — Restore `>=` in the release approval check — `approved(2, minimum=2)` returns False, so a release with exactly the required approvals is blocked. The docstring at `zzz-release/gate.py:1` says "A release needs at least the configured number of approvals", and the base compared with `>=`. — Every release holding exactly the minimum approvals, including the default of 2, is rejected, and the existing tests pass either way. — Fix: Extend `tests/test_release.py` with the `gate.approved(2, minimum=2)` boundary, which neither `test_approved_release` (3 of 2) nor `test_blocked_release` (1 of 2) exercises.

## Important
(none)

## Suggestions
- services/registry.py:88 — silent-failure — `healthy(None)` returns True where the base raised — `healthy(None)` now returns True, reporting healthy when no failure list was produced; the base `len(failures) == 0` raised `TypeError` for that input. No caller in this repository passes None, and `tests/test_release.py:19` covers only lists. — A caller that passes a missing failure result receives a healthy status with no error signal. — Fix: Keep `len(failures) == 0`, or state in a docstring that None means healthy and add that case to `test_health`.
- aaa-generated/catalog.json:6002 — correctness — Remove the non-service `review_note` entry from the catalog — The top-level `review_note` key holds a string, so a reader that iterates catalog entries and reads `port` or `enabled` fails on it. Each of the other 1500 entries maps a service name to an object with those two fields. — A consumer iterating the catalog breaks on this entry; this repository contains no catalog reader, so no in-repo failure was traced.

## Not reviewed
- `aaa-generated/catalog.json`: lines 2234–8984 of `../pr.diff` (services 0371 through 1496) were checked only by line-shape pattern counts, so name-to-port correspondence and duplicate entries in that range are unverified.
